playbook.intent: An agent has been serving real traffic on trust, and when a user reports a bad answer nobody can pull up what it actually did to produce it. It ends when a single run can be replayed step by step, a sampled slice of live traffic is scored continuously, and a shift in inputs, outputs or cost reaches an on-call engineer who has something concrete to open.
playbook.scope: Production agent goes from blind-running to fully observed: per-step OTEL traces, eval-in-prod sampling, drift detection on inputs/outputs/costs, alerting, and an on-call runbook.

success-criteria.criterion: One production run can be reconstructed from its trace alone: every model call, tool call and retry in order, each carrying its latency and token cost
A fixed share of live traffic is scored against the rubric in production, and the sampling rule is written down instead of being nudged by whoever happens to be watching
A shift in the distribution of incoming requests raises an alarm by itself, ahead of the first quality complaint from a user
Cost per successful run is tracked as a time series, so a prompt change that doubles spend is visible the day it ships rather than at the end of the month
An engineer with no prior context can follow the runbook from the alert to a decision, including the explicit point at which they are allowed to switch the agent off
Captured traces carry no raw customer data, with the sensitive fields redacted at capture time rather than scrubbed from storage afterwards
